stem.text: A function h satisfies \( \lim_{x \to \infty} h(x) = - \frac{19}{2} \). Describe in words what this statement says about h and about its graph.

answer_key.label: As x increases without bound, h(x) approaches \( - \frac{19}{2} \), so the line \( y = - \frac{19}{2} \) is a horizontal asymptote.

worked_solution.text: The input increases without bound, so the statement is about the right end of the graph only.
The outputs approach the number \( - \frac{19}{2} \) there, so the graph has the horizontal asymptote \( y = - \frac{19}{2} \) at that end.
worked_solution.rule_named: limit at infinity and horizontal asymptote

options.label: As x approaches \( - \frac{19}{2} \), h(x) increases without bound, so the line \( x = - \frac{19}{2} \) is a vertical asymptote.
options.derivation: the limit at infinity read as an infinite limit at an input, with the roles of input and output exchanged

options.label: The value of h at the input \( \infty \) is \( - \frac{19}{2} \), so the graph of h contains the point \( (\infty, - \frac{19}{2}) \).
options.derivation: infinity treated as an input at which the function takes the value

options.label: As x increases without bound, h(x) approaches \( - \frac{19}{2} \), so the line \( y = - \frac{19}{2} \) is a horizontal asymptote.
As x increases or decreases without bound, h(x) approaches \( - \frac{19}{2} \), so the line \( y = - \frac{19}{2} \) is a horizontal asymptote at both ends.
options.derivation: the statement about one end read as describing both ends of the graph
